title: IoT301 – WS6 and WS7: 150 Practice Questions

questions.prompt: A traffic light is showing green. A pedestrian presses the button. What should happen first?
choices: Green turns off, then yellow starts flashing.
Yellow and green stay on together.
questions.explanation: The WS6 sequence requires green to turn off before the yellow transition begins.

questions.prompt: The yellow light must flash for five seconds with 0.5 seconds ON and 0.5 seconds OFF. How many complete flashes are needed?
questions.explanation: One complete flash takes one second, so five flashes take five seconds.

questions.prompt: A student changes range(5) to range(3) in the yellow-light loop. How long will yellow flash?
questions.explanation: Each iteration takes one second, so three iterations take three seconds.

questions.prompt: A student writes sleep(5) instead of sleep(30) for the red period. What happens?
choices: The program waits for a button press.
questions.explanation: sleep(5) pauses the program for five seconds.

questions.prompt: Which instruction prevents a held pedestrian button from triggering another sequence?
questions.explanation: Waiting for release separates one button press from the next cycle.

questions.prompt: What is the main risk of connecting RGB channels without individual resistors?
choices: Excessive current may damage the LED or GPIO pins.
questions.explanation: Each colour channel needs current limiting.

questions.prompt: In a common-cathode RGB LED, what happens when the red GPIO output is HIGH?
questions.explanation: Common-cathode channels turn on with HIGH.

questions.prompt: What is likely when common-anode logic is used as if the LED were common-cathode?
choices: Colours may operate with inverted ON/OFF behaviour.
The Raspberry Pi ignores the LED.
questions.explanation: Common-anode logic is inverted.

questions.prompt: Which RGB value displays yellow?
questions.explanation: Yellow combines red and green.

questions.prompt: What colour should appear for led.color = (0, 1, 1)?
questions.explanation: Green and blue together produce cyan.

questions.prompt: Which channels are active in led.color = (1, 0, 1)?
questions.explanation: The first and third values are active.

questions.prompt: Which value turns an RGB LED completely off?
questions.explanation: All three channels must be zero.

questions.prompt: What does led.color = (0.5, 0, 0) mean?
questions.explanation: A channel value of 0.5 represents intermediate brightness.

questions.prompt: Which instruction displays white?
questions.explanation: White activates all three channels.

questions.prompt: What is the total resistance of 100 ohms and 200 ohms in series?
questions.explanation: Series resistance is the sum: 100 + 200 = 300 ohms.

questions.prompt: What is the approximate resistance of 100 ohms and 200 ohms in parallel?
questions.explanation: The parallel formula gives approximately 66.7 ohms.

questions.prompt: What is the best correction when green and blue RGB channels have no resistors?
choices: Add a separate resistor to green and blue.
Connect all channels directly to GND.
Use one resistor for the button.
questions.explanation: Each colour channel needs its own current-limiting resistor.

questions.prompt: What is likely if a 330-ohm resistor is replaced with much higher resistance?
choices: The LED becomes dimmer or may not light.
questions.explanation: Higher resistance reduces current and brightness.

questions.prompt: Which library supports colour names such as red and blue?
questions.explanation: colorzero provides the Color class.

questions.prompt: Which instruction sets an RGB LED to blue using Color?
questions.explanation: Color("blue") can be assigned to the color property.

questions.prompt: Which command starts the Python 3 interpreter on Raspberry Pi?
questions.explanation: python3 launches the Python 3 interpreter.

questions.prompt: In RGBLED(17, 27, 22), which channel uses GPIO27?
questions.explanation: RGBLED arguments are red, green, then blue.

questions.prompt: What changes when RGBLED(17, 22, 27) is used instead of RGBLED(17, 27, 22)?
questions.explanation: The second and third arguments represent green and blue.

questions.prompt: How many ON/OFF combinations exist for three RGB channels?
questions.explanation: There are 2^3, or eight, combinations.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of three nested loops using range(2)?
questions.explanation: Each loop controls one binary channel.

questions.prompt: What changes if time.sleep(1) becomes time.sleep(2) in the colour cycle?
questions.explanation: The delay controls display duration.

questions.prompt: Which value makes the RGB LED green by default?
questions.explanation: Green is the second channel.

questions.prompt: Which pair starts a red flashing LED and buzzer?
questions.explanation: These calls start matching red flashing and beeping.

questions.prompt: Which setting lets blink continue while the program runs the next line?
questions.explanation: background=True makes the operation non-blocking.

questions.prompt: What happens when an indefinite operation uses background=False?
choices: The program waits and may never reach the next line.
questions.explanation: A blocking indefinite operation prevents later instructions.

questions.prompt: What should the second button press do in the RGB alarm project?
choices: Stop the LED flashing and buzzer.
questions.explanation: The second press ends the alarm state.

questions.prompt: Why use wait_for_release() after a button press?
choices: It prevents a held button affecting the next press cycle.
questions.explanation: Waiting for release separates distinct presses.

questions.prompt: Which structure repeats a traffic-light sequence continuously?
questions.explanation: while True creates an infinite loop.

questions.prompt: What should happen after the final yellow transition?
questions.explanation: The WS6 sequence returns to green.

questions.prompt: What should be corrected if red remains on while yellow flashes?
choices: Turn red off before yellow starts.
questions.explanation: The stages should not overlap.

questions.prompt: Which instruction controls a 30-second red period?
questions.explanation: sleep(30) pauses while red remains on.

questions.prompt: Which testing adjustment makes the traffic-light sequence faster?
choices: Yellow delay 0.1 seconds and red duration 5 seconds.
Yellow delay 5 seconds and red duration 30 seconds.
Yellow delay 30 seconds and red duration 0.1 seconds.
questions.explanation: Short delays are suitable for testing only.

questions.prompt: What is the main logic change for a pedestrian-perspective traffic light?
choices: Invert the red and green roles.
questions.explanation: Pedestrian perspective uses the opposite default role.

questions.prompt: How long is one flash with 0.5 seconds ON and OFF?
questions.explanation: The two half-second periods total one second.

questions.prompt: What should be checked first if RGB values produce the wrong colour?
choices: RGB channel connections and GPIO assignments.
questions.explanation: The software channel order must match the wiring.

questions.prompt: Which correction uses a Color object for red?

questions.prompt: With from gpiozero import RGBLED, which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Direct import allows RGBLED without a prefix.

questions.prompt: Which instruction displays magenta?

questions.prompt: Which instruction displays cyan?

questions.prompt: Why are background operations useful in the RGB alarm?

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of led.off() and buzzer.off() after the second press?

questions.prompt: What should happen after the RGB alarm stops?
